evidence_objects.explanation: Matched units with unobstructed valley/city view list 9% above equivalent inward-facing units in the same building band.
Upper-floor premium isolated by holding view, area and finish constant.

sources.name: Dept. of Lands & Survey — Monthly Trading

evidence_objects.explanation: Listings are asking prices; calibrated to expected transaction level using the mid of the documented gap.
Streetscape and mixed-use frontage upgrade along the Abdoun corridor supports premium positioning; effect is appreciation, not applied to today's band.
Announced campus strengthens family-buyer demand over a 12–24 month horizon.

risk_factors.title: Thin luxury liquidity
risk_factors.detail: Absorption at the top of the band is slow; premium pricing depends on 1–2 comparable sales rather than a deep pool.

risk_factors.title: Ask-price dispersion
risk_factors.detail: Wide spread between aspirational and realistic listings; confidence relies on the transaction calibration holding.

Abdoun.narrative: Abdoun sits at the top of the Amman apartment market. The evidenced grid places the justified launch band at a premium to the neighbourhood median, driven by view, finish and floor, and disciplined by the ask-to-transaction calibration. Future-signal corridor and amenity upgrades support a raise-later posture rather than a reduction.

evidence_objects.explanation: Premium for plot size and privacy relative to apartment-dense comparables.
West-facing open-view units carry a measurable premium.
Newer delivery reduces depreciation drag.
Fewer within-radius amenities than inner submarkets; mild discount.

sources.name: Dept. of Lands & Survey — Monthly Trading

evidence_objects.explanation: Larger ask-gap observed for higher-ticket villa listings.
Improved arterial access shortens effective commute; appreciation driver for outer west submarkets.
Proposed neighbourhood retail centre would close the amenity gap noted in the current-state discount.

risk_factors.title: Small comparable pool
risk_factors.detail: Villa-class transactions are sparse; the band leans on a handful of listings and carries wider uncertainty.

risk_factors.title: Amenity dependency
risk_factors.detail: Value is sensitive to the future retail/services node materialising on schedule.

Dabouq.narrative: Dabouq is a low-density villa submarket where premium is a function of plot, privacy and view rather than density. Comparable liquidity is thin, so confidence is medium and the band is wider. Future arterial and retail signals underpin an appreciation story for a patient launch.

evidence_objects.explanation: High within-radius retail/F&B density supports a walkability premium.
City-facing units above the podium line.
Parking scarcity in the commercial core raises the premium for covered bays.
Units on active commercial frontage discount vs set-back residential.

sources.name: Dept. of Lands & Survey — Monthly Trading

evidence_objects.explanation: Tighter ask-gap in a liquid, transaction-rich submarket.
Feasibility-stage transit feeder; low certainty but material if delivered.
Retail-street pedestrianisation would reinforce the walkability premium.

risk_factors.title: Mixed-use noise
risk_factors.detail: Commercial frontage cuts both ways — footfall lifts retail value but discounts residential quiet.

risk_factors.title: Supply pipeline
risk_factors.detail: Steady permit issuance in the corridor could compress premiums if absorption lags.

Sweifieh.narrative: Sweifieh trades on walkability and liquidity. A transaction-rich pool gives high confidence and a tighter band. The evidenced grid rewards retail proximity and parking while discounting active-frontage noise. Transit and pedestrianisation signals support a hold-and-raise stance.

evidence_objects.explanation: Dense family-amenity cluster supports a family-buyer premium.
Modest floor premium; ceiling lower than in prime submarkets.
Semi-furnished units clear faster and list slightly higher.
Moderate depreciation for mid-age stock.

sources.name: Dept. of Lands & Survey — Monthly Trading

evidence_objects.explanation: Standard mid-market ask-gap applied.
Interchange upgrade improves connectivity for the north-west residential belt.
Planned green space would lift the amenity score of adjacent blocks.

risk_factors.title: Elastic mid-market supply
risk_factors.detail: Family mid-market has the deepest pipeline; over-pricing risks slow absorption against ample alternatives.

Khalda.narrative: Khalda is a deep, liquid family submarket. Value is driven by amenity access and unit practicality rather than luxury attributes. High comparable density gives strong confidence and a tight band; the main discipline is not over-reaching against elastic supply.

evidence_objects.explanation: Proximity to the CBD and offices supports a rental-led premium.
Above-median gross yield underpins investor demand and the sale premium.
Upper-floor city view over the district.
A share of the core is ageing; depreciation applied vs newer infill.

sources.name: Dept. of Lands & Survey — Monthly Trading

evidence_objects.explanation: Standard ask-gap; slightly tighter for investor-grade units.
Adaptive reuse trend tightens residential supply in the core.

sources.name: Central Bank of Jordan — Real Estate Price Index

evidence_objects.explanation: Time-adjustment factor from the CBJ Real Estate Price Index trends positive for Amman apartments.

risk_factors.title: Ageing core
risk_factors.detail: Mixed building vintages widen dispersion; the band assumes a mid-vintage subject.

risk_factors.title: Office-cycle sensitivity
risk_factors.detail: Demand is partly tied to the commercial office cycle.

Shmeisani.narrative: Shmeisani is a business-district submarket where yield and centrality drive value against an ageing core. Confidence is medium given vintage dispersion. Conversion pressure and a positive official index trend support the appreciation narrative behind a firm launch band.
